title: CREST-CiM: Cross-Coupling-Enhanced Differential STT-MRAM for Robust Computing-in-Memory in Binary Neural Networks
problem: Standard MRAM-based computing-in-memory suffers from low distinguishability of stored weights (+1/-1), resulting in poor sense-margin and vulnerability to process variations and hardware non-idealities.
motivation: Binary neural networks require efficient in-memory computation for edge and low-power deployment, and MRAM offers promise, but current designs lack robustness.
method: CREST-CiM stores each binary weight using two magnetic tunnel junctions—tiny devices that switch between magnetic states to encode data—connected together per memory cell, one storing +1 and one storing −1. Cross-coupling them (linking their magnetic states) dramatically increases the difference between the electrical current when reading the +1 state versus the −1 state, achieving an 8100-fold ratio. This much larger difference makes the reading circuit much more reliable, allowing it to correctly identify weights despite manufacturing variations and other hardware imperfections.
key_novelty: Linking two magnetic storage devices per weight creates an 8100-fold difference in readable current with only 7.9% additional chip area.
contributions: 3.4x higher CiM sense-margin compared to 2T-2MTJ baseline
Resilience to process variations and hardware non-idealities
Near-software accuracy on ResNet-18/CIFAR-10 with 10.7% improvement over baseline
limitations: Limited to binary neural networks; no evaluation on other network architectures or larger datasets mentioned.
primary_theme: MRAM-based computing-in-memory for binary neural networks
